item.title: Six cyberbullying victims reported to police this year, half of them minors
item.description: Home Affairs Minister Glenn Bedingfield told parliament that the police identified six alleged cyberbullying victims this year, three of them minors aged 13 and 14, with five of the six female. Four cases were registered in the police electronic system while two emerged during other investigations, and legal action was taken in two cases with charges brought in a third.
item.content:encoded:

Four cases were registered in the police electronic system while two emerged during other investigations, and legal action was taken in two cases with charges brought in a third.

Sources: Times of Malta

item.title: Constitutional Court turns away ITS lecturers' union freedom case
item.description: Two veteran Institute of Tourism Studies lecturers, disciplined after refusing to teach mixed kitchen classes they believed were unsafe, have been turned away by the Constitutional Court. Judge Abigail Lofaro ruled they should first have taken the case to the Industrial Tribunal, declining to rule on whether union recognition rules muzzle minority unions such as the Union of Professional Educators.

item.title: ERA switches 24/7 emergency line to 1404
item.description: The Environment and Resources Authority has replaced its 24/7 emergency number, 2292 3500, with the shorter 1404 so residents can report incidents needing immediate attention. Reportable incidents include waste burning, illegal dumping, unlawful cutting of trees and vegetation, illegal harvesting or trade of protected species and pollution incidents.

item.title: Villa Lauri opens in Birkirkara for Gozitan patients and relatives
item.description: Gozo Minister Clint Camilleri has inaugurated Villa Lauri, a four-storey facility with 23 rooms and 33 beds offering accommodation to Gozitan patients travelling to Malta for treatment and to the relatives accompanying them. Access is available to Gozitan residents with appointments before 10am or needing an overnight stay, with both parents allowed to accompany child patients, and applications can be made through gozo.gov.mt or the MyGozo app.

item.title: Formal education workforce up 1.3% to 20,448 staff
item.description: National Statistics Office data show total teaching and non-teaching staff in formal education reached 20,448 in the 2024-2025 academic year, with 10,664 in teaching and academic roles. Women made up 70.2% of staff, while foreign classroom teachers and academic staff rose 3.8% year on year and male staff still outnumbered women at tertiary academic level.

item.title: Jason Micallef sues Karl Schembri over Ta' Qali gravel contract comment
item.description: Jason Micallef has filed a defamation suit against author and former journalist Karl Schembri over a Facebook comment accusing him of incompetence and corruption in connection with the Ta' Qali gravel contract. The case adds to a running dispute over the gravel quarry operation and the running of the Mtaħleb quarry in the Wied iż-Żurien area.

item.title: Government launches 10-year National Cycling Strategy 2026–2036
item.description: The government unveiled a ten-year cycling strategy on Wednesday aimed at making the bicycle a safer and more practical form of everyday transport in Malta and Gozo. The National Cycling Strategy 2026–2036 proposes a nationwide network of cycling routes linking residential areas with schools, workplaces and public transport hubs, along with improved bicycle parking and training programmes for children and adults. It is built on five pillars — infrastructure, facilities, road safety and enforcement, education, and incentives — and replaces a 2018 action plan that was originally due for completion in 2023.

item.title: Four Heritage Malta workers charged over alleged duplicate-ticket scam
item.description: Four Heritage Malta employees were arraigned in court on Wednesday accused of exploiting a ticketing loophole to sell duplicate tickets and pocket the cash. CCTV footage showed workers printing the same valid ticket up to eight times, hiding copies inside promotional leaflets and handing them to unsuspecting visitors who paid in cash. The accused are Ryan Bonnici, Brian Castillo, Tonio Cauchi and Godwin Joseph Zarb; the latter three remain suspended from duty pending the outcome of the criminal proceedings.

item.title: Abela at COP31: offshore solar and grid upgrades among Malta's energy plans
item.description: Prime Minister Robert Abela told the COP31 climate summit in Antalya that Malta would strengthen energy security through national grid improvements and greater investment in renewable projects, including offshore technologies and the potential development of offshore solar photovoltaic installations. He said Malta's National Climate Resilience Plan would be developed further in 2027, with targeted actions across ten vulnerable sectors including energy, water, healthcare, transport and food security.

item.title: Blood testing at health centres to proceed despite doctors' objections
item.description: Health Minister Ian Borg told parliament that point-of-care blood testing in health centres will go ahead despite reservations from the Medical Association of Malta, saying the decision itself is not open to debate. The MAM fears the scheme could delay treatment for seriously ill patients and add pressure to overstretched health centres, while the minister argues it will reduce unnecessary visits to Mater Dei's emergency department.

item.title: Culture minister says he 'could have used better words' after artists' backlash
item.description: Culture Minister Malcolm Paul Agius Galea acknowledged that his remarks about artists may have come across as insensitive, saying he "could have used better words". The comments — recorded at the Festival of Ideas and leaked to Times of Malta — triggered a furious reaction in the arts sector, with lobby groups demanding his resignation and thousands signing a petition. Asked whether he intended to resign, the minister said he would shoulder responsibility by working harder for the culture sector.

item.title: Caruana refuses to publish eight-year-old population growth report
item.description: Finance Minister Clyde Caruana again refused to publish a report he submitted to government eight years ago on the impact of rapid population growth on national sectors, saying he was its author but not its destination. Asked in parliament by shadow minister Adrian Delia whether he was being prevented from releasing it, Caruana said the government had already acted on population concerns in the Budget and was realigning the economy towards capital and technology rather than human resources.

item.title: €5 million Criminal Court of Appeal building taking shape in Valletta
item.description: A €5.1 million building for Malta's Criminal Court of Appeal on Triq id-Dejqa in Valletta is under construction, with three new courtrooms, offices for the judiciary and administrative staff, registry and archive space, and a dedicated area for victims. The Justice Ministry said work is progressing despite the challenges of building in Valletta's historic centre, and that the project will free up room in the main law courts for additional hearings.

item.title: Malta Book Festival attracts record 43,400 visitors
item.description: The Malta Book Festival at the Malta Fairs and Conventions Centre in Ta' Qali drew a record 43,400 visitors, up from 40,000 last year, the Arts and Culture Ministry said. Schoolchildren redeemed 19,000 book vouchers worth €20 each, generating €380,000 in purchases from local publishers and booksellers.

item.title: Metsola: EU rules must reflect realities of island businesses
item.description: European Parliament President Roberta Metsola told a delegation of Maltese business lobbyists that EU policies which make it harder for island businesses to compete must be reconsidered. Speaking to the Malta Business Bureau, which marked its 30th anniversary, she said policymakers must take account of the particular challenges of island economies such as Malta and Gozo, including the impact of the EU Emissions Trading System on air and maritime links.

item.title: Man granted electronic-tagging bail over alleged domestic violence
item.description: A 22-year-old man was granted bail with electronic monitoring after being charged with domestic violence offences, including causing slight injuries to his former partner and breaching bail conditions imposed in 2023 and last month. The case surfaced on 6 November, when Isla Local Council passed on a neighbour's video apparently showing the accused grabbing a woman by the hair and dragging her from a balcony.

item.title: 217 children in foster care in Malta, 25 still awaiting a family
item.description: Some 217 children currently live with foster families in Malta, while 25 young people who have turned 18 still live with the families that took them in, Social Policy and Family Minister Michael Falzon said at an FSWS conference. The event, themed on adverse childhood experiences, brought together professionals and foster carers to discuss the effects of traumatic experiences in childhood and the therapeutic value of stable care.

item.title: Airport records 85% seat occupancy with 1.05 million passengers in October
item.description: Malta International Airport welcomed about 1.05 million passengers in October, with seat occupancy at 84.7% and aircraft movements up 6.6% year on year across more than 110 destinations. The UK led the market with a 21% share, followed by Italy and Poland, while France recorded a 12.3% drop after two routes were discontinued. MIA expects winter traffic to remain broadly unchanged, with high fuel prices weighing on airlines.

item.title: Birżebbuġa council petitions parliament over Hal Far fish-processing odours
item.description: The Birżebbuġa Local Council is urging residents to sign a petition asking parliament to act on persistent odours from fish processing at the Ħal Far industrial estate, a problem first flagged in 2022. The petition, launched with Għaqda Storja u Kultura Birżebbuġa and Moviment Graffitti, is addressed to Environment Minister Miriam Dalli and Lands Minister Silvio Schembri.

item.title: Man acquitted of Paola truck arson over CCTV chain-of-custody gap
item.description: A 47-year-old man was acquitted of setting fire to a truck in Paola after Magistrate Nadine Sant Lia ruled that CCTV footage linking him to the Kia Picanto involved could not be considered because of a break in the chain of custody. Investigators had traced the car to Darren Spiteri, but the court found the prosecution had not proved he was driving it or started the fire in February 2024, which damaged a garage and an apartment block.

item.title: University staff association urges exemption from TCN budget measures
item.description: The University of Malta Academic Staff Association has written to Education Minister Byron Camilleri asking that non-European staff be exempted from budget measures including the removal of free childcare and public transport, higher driving licence fees and a €400 infrastructure contribution. UMASA says the measures place a significant additional burden on third-country nationals working in Malta, while the Malta Union of Midwives and Nurses has made a similar request for healthcare workers.

item.title: Ryanair marks 20 years in Malta with 53 routes this winter
item.description: Ryanair is celebrating two decades of operating in Malta, having launched its first two routes to London Luton and Pisa in October 2006. The airline will run nearly 300 weekly flights across 53 routes this winter from a base of nine aircraft at Malta International Airport, connecting the island with the UK, France, Spain, Italy and Poland among other markets.

item.title: Non-EU students face at least €1,200 in fees under Budget 2027 bill
item.description: Bill 15 would raise the residence permit fee for third-country national students from €50 to €500, increase service visa fees and add a €400 annual infrastructure contribution, taking the minimum cost for an adult student to about €1,200. The changes follow a wider package of fee increases targeting third-country nationals, including employment permits rising from €600 to €800.

item.title: Repubblika demands independent probe into alleged vote-buying via public jobs
item.description: Civil society organisation Repubblika has called for an independent investigation into allegations that public sector recruitment was used to secure votes during the election campaign, backing a police report filed by lawyer and former Nationalist MP Jason Azzopardi. Repubblika says the police claim they found evidence contradicting the allegations, but questions the lack of information about what was examined.

item.title: One survivor out of coma, 14-year-old still critical after boat collision
item.description: Daniel Buttigieg, 44, has come out of a coma following the boat crash on a reef off Baħar ic-Ċagħaq and is talking to friends, while 14-year-old Ben Caruana Rizzo remains stable but has "a long way to go", according to family. Their friend Keith Caruana, 48, from Mellieħa, suffered fatal injuries in the Sunday incident. The family has asked supporters to keep sending messages of encouragement to the two survivors still in hospital.

item.title: Temu and Shein shoppers face a further €2 handling fee
item.description: Shoppers using low-cost platforms such as Temu and Shein now face an extra €2 handling levy that took effect on 1 November, on top of the €3 customs tax introduced in July on low-value goods bought outside the EU. Times of Malta asked shoppers in Valletta whether the charges would deter them, with mixed responses: some said the sites were no longer worth it, while others said they would still buy when needed.

item.title: Central Bank study: accommodation and food sector worth €1.15bn, more reliant on foreign workers
item.description: A Central Bank of Malta analysis by economist Eliza Farrugia found the accommodation and food services sector generated €1.15 billion in gross value added in 2025, or 6.3% of economic output, with 4,297 active business units in 2024. The sector added 1,911 units between 2015 and 2024 and remains dominated by micro firms, but the study flags low wages, weak productivity and heavy reliance on transient foreign labour.

item.title: OPM denies ever receiving the 300-page population growth report
item.description: The office of the prime minister has said the population report commissioned in 2017 was never presented to cabinet or to Robert Abela, contradicting Finance Minister Clyde Caruana's account that he repeatedly warned government about the effects of rapid population growth. The OPM spokesperson said the document appears to have reached Joseph Muscat personally but never Muscat's cabinet, while Caruana maintains it was completed in late 2018 and shelved first by the 2019 MEP election and then by the pandemic. The exchange continues in parliament after Caruana declined to table the report earlier this week.

item.title: Third attempt to develop Mosta ODZ site with padel courts, restaurant and gym
item.description: A proposal to develop padel courts, a restaurant and a gym opposite the Durumblat cemetery in Mosta marks the third attempt to build on the site outside the development zone. The application was published on MaltaToday on Wednesday morning, restarting consideration of the ODZ plot.
